layers.title: Platform foundation
layers.summary: The common base that product workflows use for intelligence, shared services and a consistent data model.

nodes.label: AI Platform
nodes.summary: Provides the governed AI runtime and services that bring model assistance and agent capabilities into ServiceNow workflows.
nodes.detail: Product maps place the AI Platform beneath the application. It supplies shared AI services so Now Assist, AI agents and predictive capabilities can operate in workflow context.

nodes.label: Core Services
nodes.summary: Shared platform services that support application behavior, access, automation and administration.
nodes.detail: Core Services sit beneath product-specific applications. They provide the common platform capabilities that teams configure and extend across workflows.

nodes.label: Single Data Model
nodes.summary: A common record and relationship foundation that helps workflows share operational context.
nodes.detail: Product architectures show a shared data model beneath applications. Connected records help preserve context across teams, services and system handoffs.

layers.title: Shared platform services
layers.summary: Cross-cutting services are reused by multiple product portfolios. Select a service to see what it contributes and which portfolios it supports.

nodes.label: User Experience
nodes.summary: Provides the channels and workspaces where employees, agents, customers and technicians interact with services.
nodes.detail: The map treats experience channels as shared entry points. The channel can change while the request, service context and work continue through the platform.
offerings: Customer-facing self-service entry for questions, cases and service requests.
A shared employee entry point for finding information, requesting services and following progress.
Conversational self-service that can answer questions or start workflow actions.
In-person service intake and support for locations that offer staffed assistance.
Mobile access for people who need service or task information away from a desktop.
Role-based work areas that bring tasks, context and actions together for service teams.
Digital conversations connected to service work and case handling.

nodes.label: Analytics
nodes.summary: Measures workflow performance and helps teams understand process behavior, bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.
nodes.detail: Analytics and process analysis appear as shared capabilities across the portfolio. Teams use operational data to monitor service levels, identify friction and evaluate whether changes improve outcomes.
offerings: Indicators and dashboards used to monitor workflow performance.
Process analysis that helps locate delays, rework and variation.
Task-level insight used to understand manual work patterns.
Signals about digital experience that can help teams find points of friction.
Structured work for identifying, prioritizing and tracking process improvements.

nodes.label: AI
nodes.summary: AI capabilities assist people, predict outcomes and support agents inside governed workflows.
nodes.detail: AI is shown as a shared layer across product architectures. The specific use depends on the workflow, available data, model configuration, security controls and human review points.
offerings: Generative AI experiences embedded in ServiceNow workflows.
Build and coordinate task-focused agents that use approved tools and workflow context.
Machine-learning capabilities for classification, prediction and recommendations.
Configurable guardrails and monitoring for AI interactions.
Extract and classify information from documents for downstream work.
Search across relevant enterprise knowledge and content.
Reusable AI actions that can be made available in workflow experiences.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.summary: Connects records, service context and external data so workflows and AI can use relevant information.
nodes.detail: Data capabilities include the shared operational model and ways to discover or connect information held in other systems. Teams should identify authoritative sources and define access and freshness requirements.
offerings: Connect enterprise data and applications to workflows, analytics and AI.
Maintain configuration and service relationships used for impact and ownership context.
Bring supported third-party data into Service Graph and CMDB structures.
Provide access to supported external data without first copying it into the platform.
Organize service knowledge for search and self-service.
Present defined services and request choices through guided channels.

nodes.label: Workflow
nodes.summary: Coordinates tasks, approvals, routing and exceptions so work moves between teams with ownership and status.
nodes.detail: Workflow capabilities provide the process layer. They connect an intake or signal to accountable work, route tasks, manage decisions and expose the state of the process.
offerings: Design and manage workflow logic and process actions.
Route work to the appropriate agent or queue based on configured criteria.
Connect a request across service teams while preserving a consistent requester experience.
Create guided decision paths for service interactions.
Test configured applications and workflows to support release confidence.
Define and monitor service commitments and performance.

nodes.label: Integration Services
nodes.summary: Connects workflows with external applications, APIs, event streams and automation actions.
nodes.detail: Integration services allow work to cross system boundaries. Reusable spokes, APIs and automation patterns reduce one-off handoffs while keeping process ownership visible in ServiceNow.
offerings: Use reusable spokes and actions to connect workflow steps with external systems.
Coordinate integrations, robotic process automation and related automation capabilities.
Connect supported event streams with platform workflows.
Make supported external content discoverable in relevant experiences.
Connect API management capabilities to integration workflows.
Move data through supported import, export and embedded connection patterns.

nodes.label: Security & Trust
nodes.summary: Applies identity, access, data protection and governance controls across applications and workflows.
nodes.detail: Security and trust capabilities are common controls in the architecture. Configuration determines who can see or act on records, how data is protected and how exceptions are handled.
offerings: Control access to records and actions through permissions and role assignments.
Centralize security posture and related operational visibility.
Add another verification step to supported sign-in flows.
Separate data and administration boundaries in supported multitenant designs.
Protect selected platform data using supported encryption and key-management controls.
Connect supported directory services for identity-related processes.
Apply supported file scanning and access-control patterns.

layers.title: Applications & workflow portfolios
layers.summary: Product portfolios organize shared platform capabilities around the work teams need to complete.

nodes.label: CRM
nodes.summary: Customer-facing workflows for service, field work and sales or order processes.
nodes.detail: The customer portfolio connects a customer need to case handling, fulfillment and related commercial work. A customer case may cross into IT, field service or core operations depending on the process.
offerings: Manage customer cases across channels and coordinate back-office fulfillment.
Plan and deliver customer-facing field work, dispatch and technician execution.
Manage lead, quote, order and fulfillment processes.
Configure offers and support pricing and quoting processes.
Give customers a digital channel to find help and follow service work.

nodes.label: IT
nodes.summary: Technology service, operations, asset and portfolio workflows for enterprise IT.
nodes.detail: The IT portfolio spans service delivery, operations visibility, technology architecture and asset lifecycle management. Shared CMDB and service context help teams assess impact and coordinate response.
offerings: Manage incidents, problems, changes, requests and knowledge.
Discover technology, monitor services and coordinate operational response.
Manage software and hardware assets through their lifecycle.
Manage maintenance and lifecycle work for physical assets.
Connect strategy, investment, demand, planning and delivery.
Model business and technology architecture to guide investment and change.
Monitor and improve employee technology experiences.
Provide operational service and configuration context.

nodes.label: OT
nodes.summary: Operational technology workflows for visibility, asset lifecycle, service operations and vulnerability response.
nodes.detail: OT capabilities extend service management patterns to operational environments. Visibility and asset context support issue response, maintenance planning and risk reduction while respecting operational constraints.
offerings: Coordinate service work for operational technology environments.
Discover and maintain visibility into operational technology assets.
Manage the operational lifecycle of OT assets.
Prioritize and coordinate remediation of OT vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: Security & Risk
nodes.summary: Security operations, resilience, compliance, privacy and third-party risk workflows.
nodes.detail: This portfolio helps organizations turn findings, assessments and control gaps into accountable work. Prioritization can use asset, service, business impact and ownership context.
offerings: Coordinate security incident response and vulnerability remediation.
Manage risk, audit, policy and compliance processes.
Assess and monitor supplier and partner risk through the relationship lifecycle.
Manage privacy requests, impact assessments and breach workflows.
Plan, test and coordinate response and recovery work.
Provide governance and visibility for AI assets and use cases.
Manage ESG data, reporting and related work.

nodes.label: Core Business Suite
nodes.summary: Employee, workplace, legal, sourcing and financial operations for the organization.
nodes.detail: Core business workflows coordinate work in functions beyond IT and customer service. A shared service experience can provide consistent access while each function keeps its process ownership and controls.
offerings: Deliver employee services through cases, knowledge and lifecycle workflows.
Coordinate workplace services, facilities work and space experiences.
Manage workplace safety cases, incidents and related actions.
Coordinate legal requests, matters and contract operations.
Manage procurement requests and sourcing work.
Support supplier onboarding, information and lifecycle tasks.
Coordinate invoice processing and accounts payable work.

nodes.label: Application Development
nodes.summary: Tools and services for building platform applications, extending workflows and managing developer work.
nodes.detail: Application development connects platform foundations with organization-specific processes. Teams can start with low-code tools and add governed integrations, testing and AI-supported development as needed.
offerings: Build workflow applications with platform data and services.
Extend ERP-related processes with platform workflows.
Create applications using a guided development experience.
Use AI assistance in app creation and developer workflows.
Use agent capabilities within supported application-development tasks.
Create user interfaces for web and mobile workflow experiences.
Separate development and experimentation from production work.

layers.title: Industry solutions
layers.summary: Industry solutions apply shared platform services and workflow portfolios to sector-specific operating models.

nodes.label: Financial Services
nodes.summary: Banking and insurance workflows for customer lifecycle operations, financial products, service and risk.
nodes.detail: The industry map and product examples show customer servicing alongside financial product operations such as cards, payments, loans, deposits and insurance. That creates a clear connection to CRM and Core Business workflows; IT and Security & Risk support the technology and control work around those services.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Customer servicing and financial customer lifecycle examples connect directly to CRM workflows.
relationships.portfolio-it: Financial services product maps show IT service work as an adjacent operational foundation for customer and financial workflows.
relationships.portfolio-risk: The financial services map includes risk-sensitive work, making Security & Risk a relevant connected portfolio.
relationships.portfolio-core: Financial products and operations such as card, payment, loan and deposit servicing connect to core business processes.

nodes.label: Telecom, Media & Technology
nodes.summary: Customer, network and service workflows for telecom, media and technology providers.
nodes.detail: The telecom maps connect customer service with telecom service operations, network inventory, topology, assurance and service management. CRM and IT are explicit portfolio neighbors; OT becomes relevant where operational technology services are in scope.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Telecom service and customer experience maps include customer service and customer-facing workflows.
relationships.portfolio-it: Telecom product maps include IT service management, service operations and network service context.
relationships.portfolio-ot: The overview groups OT visibility and service management with telecom and technology operating environments.
relationships.portfolio-appdev: The capability overview groups Application Development in the same telecom, media and technology solution context.

nodes.label: Technology Service Providers
nodes.summary: Service delivery and operational capabilities for organizations that provide technology services.
nodes.detail: The provider map centers on service delivery, customer context and operational service assurance. Its strongest portfolio connections are CRM and IT; OT and security are shown as adjacent capabilities for providers with those operational and risk needs.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Provider service journeys include customer, account and service relationship work.
relationships.portfolio-it: Service providers rely on IT service operations and service assurance capabilities shown in the provider map.
relationships.portfolio-ot: The overview connects provider operating models to OT service management and visibility where operational environments apply.
relationships.portfolio-risk: Security and risk capabilities are adjacent to the provider service and assurance operating model.

nodes.label: Public Sector
nodes.summary: Digital public services and internal workflows for government organizations.
nodes.detail: The public sector map includes constituent-facing digital services, government agent experiences and digital permits, supported by IT service workflows. This connects the sector to CRM and IT portfolios without implying that every agency uses the same solution set.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Constituent experience, service requests and public-facing digital services align with customer-service workflows.
relationships.portfolio-it: The public sector map explicitly includes IT service workflows supporting agency operations.

nodes.label: Manufacturing
nodes.summary: Commercial, service and operational workflows across manufacturing and connected assets.
nodes.detail: Manufacturing examples include configurable offers, product hierarchy, order-to-cash, dealer and channel work, post-sales service, warranty and recalls. CRM and Core Business are explicit commercial connections; IT, OT and application development support related technology and plant workflows where used.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Post-sales service, dealer and channel processes connect manufacturing to customer-facing workflows.
relationships.portfolio-it: IT service and asset workflows support the technology environment around manufacturing operations.
relationships.portfolio-ot: The overview includes OT service and asset capabilities for operational environments; detailed manufacturing examples can connect plant work where deployed.
relationships.portfolio-core: Order-to-cash, product hierarchy, commercial operations, warranty and recall processes link to core business workflows.
relationships.portfolio-appdev: The overview groups Application Development with manufacturing solutions for extending workflows to specific operating needs.

nodes.label: Retail
nodes.summary: Store support and customer-service workflows for retail and hospitality operations.
nodes.detail: Retail examples include store issue management, retail case types, multistore support and retail portals. These map directly to CRM and IT service work; Core Business capabilities can support employee and workplace processes around store operations.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Retail customer cases and service experiences align with customer service workflows.
relationships.portfolio-it: Store issue management and IT service examples connect store operations with IT support.
relationships.portfolio-core: Employee and workplace service processes can support store teams and locations.

nodes.label: Healthcare
nodes.summary: Healthcare operations and service workflows for providers and life sciences organizations.
nodes.detail: Healthcare maps combine patient and healthcare data context, healthcare operations and IT service work. CRM and IT are relevant portfolio links for service experiences and operational support; shared data and security remain platform-wide concerns.

relationships.portfolio-crm: Patient and healthcare service experiences connect to customer-service workflow patterns.
relationships.portfolio-it: The healthcare map explicitly includes IT service management as operational support for healthcare organizations.

notes.relationshipModel: The four levels describe architecture and portfolio context. Shared services are cross-cutting; industry links show examples from the industry maps and do not imply a required product sequence or a license bundle.
notes.experienceChannels: Channels such as portals, mobile, workspaces, Virtual Agent and chat can appear across more than one portfolio. Their placement under User Experience describes their role as entry points rather than an exclusive product family.
